transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi... yeah, thank you. Um, I came in because, well, my brain just feels like it completely stalls out. I don't really know how else to describe it, but it's becoming a huge problem at work. I work as an engineering technologist, so I'm usually, you know, constantly looking at specs and drafting and doing quality checks. I have a bachelor's in this, I know my job inside and out, I've done it a million times. But lately... I'll just sit there at my desk. I'll have a test report open on my monitor, or honestly, even just a really, really simple CAD note that needs a minor update, and I'll just stare at it for an hour. Or longer, sometimes. And I just... I can't decide what the next sentence should be. I can't even figure out what checkbox I'm supposed to click. It's like the gears just freeze up entirely, and I sit there trying to force myself to just type a single word, or make one tiny decision about a dimension or a material grade, and I just can't make the choice. I just sit there frozen while the clock ticks.
Can you tell me if you’ve been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy along with these problems at work?

Yeah, I... I definitely have. It’s actually bleeding into literally everything else in my life, not just my job. Like, I used to be so passionate about my hobbies outside of work. I have this really nice 3D printer setup for making miniatures, and I would spend my weekends calibrating it, getting the resin just right, painting all the tiny little details... I loved it, it was my creative outlet. But my printer for miniatures has just been sitting there with the exact same half-finished figure on the build plate for months now. I haven't touched it. I walk past it every single day in my apartment and I just... I don't care. I don't even have the urge to clean it up or put the resin away. 

And it's not just the technical hobbies that I've dropped, either. Even the things I used to do just to unwind and take care of myself... like, I used to love doing yoga, or just going for a long walk in the woods near my place to get some fresh air and clear my head away from all the screens. But now? Even yoga or walking in the woods just feels like another task instead of something I actually want to do. It feels like a chore, honestly, like doing the dishes or taking out the trash. I'll think about rolling out my mat, or putting on my hiking boots to go outside, and the thought just makes me feel so incredibly exhausted and heavy. It's like my brain processes fun things as just more work. So I just don't do them. I just sit there on the couch. It's like the color is completely gone from everything I used to actually care about...
Have you ever experienced a period of time before this one—lasting at least a couple of weeks—where you felt down, lost interest in things, or had trouble functioning like this?

No, I don't... I don't think so. I mean, I've had times where I was stressed out, obviously, like when I was finishing up my bachelor's degree. That was a really intense time, especially my final year. We had this capstone project where my group had to design and prototype an automated sorting mechanism, and the deadlines were just brutal. I remember staying up until three or four in the morning for weeks on end, drinking way too much coffee, and just feeling completely burned out. I was definitely miserable then, and I probably skipped a few yoga classes because I was just too tired, but... but that was different, you know? Like, I was stressed, but I still cared. I still wanted the project to succeed, I still wanted to get a good grade, and once it was over, I bounced right back. I went back to normal. 

But this... what's happening right now... this feels completely different. It's not like I'm just tired from working too hard, because honestly, I'm barely getting any work done at all right now, like I said. And it's never dragged on like this before. It's been going on for a while now, and it just feels like this heavy, suffocating blanket that won't lift. I've never had a time in my life where I just completely stopped caring about everything, where I couldn't even make a simple decision about a CAD drawing, or where looking at my 3D printer just made me feel absolutely nothing. So, no, I've never experienced anything like this before. This is entirely new, and it's honestly really terrifying because I don't know how to snap out of it. I keep waiting for the stress to pass like it did in college, but there isn't even any real stress causing this, it's just... it's just happening to me, and it won't stop.
Have you ever had a period in your life before this current one where you felt persistently down or lost interest in things for a couple of weeks or more, even if there wasn’t a clear reason for it?

Wait, isn't that... I mean, like I was just trying to say, no. I really haven't. I know sometimes people have this kind of thing happen a lot, like it comes and goes in phases throughout their life, but for me, looking back at my whole life—even high school, middle school, all through my bachelor's—I was always the person who had a plan and a drive. I was always the one organizing the study groups, or figuring out the logistics for weekend trips with my friends, or jumping into new hobbies. 

Even when things were incredibly boring or tedious, I never just lost interest in everything for weeks on end for no reason. Like, I remember one summer between semesters I had to work this really awful data entry job just to pay for my textbooks and my rent, and it was completely mind-numbing. I was literally just typing numbers from printed, coffee-stained invoices into this ancient legacy database for eight hours a day in a windowless room. It was terrible. But even then, doing something so incredibly dull, I didn't feel *down* or empty like this. I still looked forward to going home and watching movies, or working on my 3D modeling, or seeing my friends. I still had my spark, I guess you could call it. I always had something I cared about.

So, no, to answer your question again, there has never been a time before this current stretch where I just felt persistently down or lost interest without a reason. This is the very first time my brain has ever just... shut off and refused to turn back on. It's completely out of left field for me, which is why I'm sitting here talking to you, because I just don't have a history of feeling this way and I don't know what to do with it.

Have you ever had a time in your life before this current period where you experienced a low mood or loss of interest that was so severe it significantly affected your daily life, like your ability to work, study, or interact with others, even if it was just for a couple of weeks?

I feel like we're going in circles here, honestly. Like I've been trying to explain... no. Never. I mean, I know you have to ask these things thoroughly, but I really, truly have never had anything like this happen before. Not even close. 

I was thinking about it just now while you were asking, trying to really dig deep and see if maybe I was forgetting something from high school or something, but... no. Even when I was a teenager and everything felt like the end of the world, you know how teenagers are, it never stopped me from functioning. I was always the girl who had her planner color-coded, who was juggling robotics club and AP classes and still managing to hang out with friends on the weekends. I never had a period where I couldn't get out of bed, or where I couldn't focus on my studies, or where I just pushed all my friends away because I didn't care anymore. 

Even when I had my first big breakup in my sophomore year of college—which devastated me at the time, I cried for like three days straight—I still went to my classes. I still turned in my lab reports. I still went to the dining hall and sat with my roommates, even if I was just picking at my food. It didn't derail my life, you know? It didn't seep into my ability to function as a human being. 

But right now? I can't even open a basic CAD file without feeling completely overwhelmed and just staring at the screen until my eyes blur. I haven't texted my best friend back in over a week, and she's probably worried sick, but I just can't bring myself to type out a response. It's like my whole system has just crashed. So, to be absolutely clear, because I want to make sure I'm answering you properly... no. I have never, ever had a time in my life before this where I felt this low or lost interest so severely that it messed with my work, my school, or my relationships. This is a complete first for me, and it's why I'm so desperate to figure out what's wrong.
